title: Cross-sectional survey of the care situation for patients with peripheral facial palsy
summary: Approximately 29–57 out of every 100,000 people suffer from peripheral facial palsy, a condition that typically causes paralysis on one side of the face. Facial nerve palsy can have many different causes and may be accompanied by difficulties such as incomplete eyelid closure and, as a result, dry eyes, problems with eating and drinking, as well as social limitations due to a lack of facial expression. The care situation for people with peripheral facial palsy is not standardized and has gaps. This study aims to assess the care received by people with peripheral facial palsy based on patients' reports collected through questionnaires. Among other things, the questionnaires are designed to determine which medical treatments, therapies, medications, and assistive devices the affected individuals have received; which measures were implemented during which phase of the disease; what their quality of life is like; and which needs were not met. The results are intended to provide insights into the current care situation as well as gaps during treatment.

interventions.name: Cross-sectional survey of people with peripheral facial palsy on their healthcare experiences and care pathways

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
We include patients aged 18 or older with periphery facial palsy.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals who do not have sufficient German language skills to fully understand the questionnaire (below level B2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) will be excluded.
